title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1968-08-21
lineage: Dat (Sony PCM-R500) > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/44; Edited & Mastered in Audacity by Joe Noel: Wave > Flac 16/44; Checksum & tags created in xACT; the original version of this source was off pitch; please don't circulate that version
source: SBD > Master Reels > Dat; Charlie Miller

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a classic ’68 Fillmore West show, highlighted by a monster Alligator and a smoking St. Stephen > The Eleven sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller/Noel transfer delivers a clean, crisp soundboard recording that fans rave about for its clarity and balanced mix, despite a brief diginoise glitch on Alligator and a slightly off early‑set balance. Musically the concert is a showcase of late‑summer ’68 energy – Alligator roars, St. Stephen is razor‑tight, The Eleven smokes, and Death Don't Have a Heart closes strong – making it one of the most compelling shows of that era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both performance and audio, noting only minor recording glitches; the show is consistently described as a standout ’68 gig.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with excellent snare definition on The Eleven; stream‑friendly and well‑mastered. Minor issues: ~1 s diginoise on Alligator (16:41) and slightly off balance early in the set.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑set show with a jam‑heavy first set (highlighted by Alligator) and a historic second set featuring the first known St. Stephen → The Eleven pairing, delivering strong momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s short‑lived Les Paul tone is praised; his lead work on the jams and The Eleven shines.
band_member_comments.Drums: Snare intro on The Eleven noted; a middle jam featuring just Garcia and drums receives special mention.
